The supplied header, `**Amend-grant:** fund 1 fix rounds`, funds **one** further fix round; it does not grant permission to amend the spec. The supplied ledger has spent zero funded rounds. The escalation model is already resolved to `<configured-impl-model>`.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps everything Before kept and additionally lands the literal `budget: 1 of 1 spent` line between Problem: and the file finding, which Before only paraphrased in prose. Both outputs run exactly one funded fix on <configured-impl-model> with async false, scoped tests, a single re-review, and stop without granting more or committing. Two things in After are worth tightening so the one-round fact does not drift in neighbouring cases: (1) the extra `delegate` grant-decode subagent is dispatched even though the header is supplied verbatim and the prose immediately says 'The supplied header is exactly ... so N = 1' — the wording should let the parent read a verbatim-available header directly and only delegate when it is not in hand, otherwise a judge may count this as an unrequested dispatch; (2) the funded-dispatch paragraph claims it 'does not set context: fresh' and 'carries no prior-patch path' while the payload embeds a prior review report path and runs in a fresh detached snapshot worktree — the wording should state plainly that the funded round reuses the escalated payload on the committed current-tree snapshot (RP_TREE) and that only the review report, not a patch, is carried. Also pin the delta path (`<Artifacts dir>/worktree-diffs/...`) to the actual subagent output location so 'current-tree repair context' is unambiguous.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After moves one-round and spent-line from fails to holds while keeping no-complete: Before refused to dispatch anything (missing fix-loop reference and prior tree ID), so no funded fix ran and no 'budget: 1 of 1 spent' line appeared; After dispatches exactly one funded repair with `model: "<configured-impl-model>"`, `async: false`, on a committed snapshot of the current integrated tree, runs the scoped `node --test frame.test.mjs` gate, dispatches one wave-reviewer re-review, then stops without granting another escalation or convergence exception, and the stop note places `budget: 1 of 1 spent` directly after `Problem:` and before the `src/frame.ts:21` finding. Two things in After are extraneous and risk diluting the single-round reading: the preliminary funding-confirmation `subagent` lookup (the header is supplied verbatim, so no dispatch is needed to decode it) and the `worktree: true` / `concurrency: 4` options on the repair call, which sit oddly with the explicit snapshot `cwd`. Keeping the Change intact, the wording that stays safest is: treat the supplied `**Amend-grant:**` header as read directly, dispatch the funded repair with only `async: false`, `cwd: <snapshot>`, `model: <implModel>`, then gate, re-review, observation line, and the stop note in the `Problem:` → `budget:` → finding order After already uses.
